findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) can attach the wrong ID to an event
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi` deduplicates ids and returns a dict (`src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:174-199`). It can omit missing nodes or return them in a different order than requested. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` then pairs IDs with the wrong event data once any node is missing or any ID is duplicated. The summary would show the wrong errors with no error raised. Iterate `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and use `events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Error timestamps and replay event timestamps are probably in different units
findings.body: Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, where `timestamp` is epoch seconds as a float (line 115). Replay recording events use the rrweb `timestamp`, which is epoch milliseconds (`as_log_message` reads `event.get("timestamp")` at `event_parser.py:182`). The merge loop at lines 153-155 compares the two directly. If the units differ, every error is emitted before the first replay event, so the chronological interleaving is wrong. The timestamp printed in the error log message would also be in seconds while the breadcrumb timestamps are in milliseconds. Normalize one side, for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000, and add a test with realistic timestamps.

findings.title: Error IDs are not bounded before the nodestore fetch
findings.body: `error_ids` comes straight from the replay row and is passed in full to `get_multi`. A replay with many errors causes a large nodestore read and a large Seer payload. Consider capping the number of IDs.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity is not enforced
findings.body: The validators use truthiness of `initial_data`. `age=0` together with a `timestamp` passes, because `0` is falsy. A report with neither field also validates, even though one of the two specs requires one of them. Use `"age" in initial_data` for the exclusivity check, and add a `validate()` method that requires exactly one of the fields.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization renders with empty columns and data
findings.body: Behind `use-table-widget-visualization`, the widget gets `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`, so it never shows the query results. This is fine only if the flag stays off. If it is enabled for anyone, dashboard table widgets render empty. Add a TODO or leave the path out until it is wired to `result.data` and `result.meta`.

findings.title: get_environment_info does a nodestore fetch per issue
findings.body: `get_recommended_event()` runs a query and a nodestore fetch for each issue in the comment. It sits inside a list comprehension in both the GitHub and GitLab workflows. The broad `except` hides failures, and they are logged only at info level.

findings.title: Flagged table path renders an empty table, ignoring result data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` gets `columns={[]}` and empty `data`/`meta`, so the widget shows no data. `result.data`, `result.meta` and `loading` are dropped, and the loading placeholder is lost on this path. I found no registration of this flag under `src`, so it can't be turned on through the normal feature system yet. If it is a placeholder, a TODO would make that clear. If the flag is ever enabled, dashboard table widgets go blank.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is only applied while a search query is entered
findings.body: The early return at line 61-63 (`if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;`) runs before the new `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check at line 67. With an empty search, which is the default view, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown. They are hidden only once the user types something. Apply the hidden filter before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes.filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name)))`.

findings.title: Possible transient 'Project not found' error while projects load
findings.body: `useProjectFromId` returns undefined until `useProjects()` has the project in its list (static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:7-13). The new branch shows an error Alert whenever `replayRecord.project_id` is set and the project is not found, without checking whether projects are still loading. If the project store is not yet populated, users may briefly see a permanent-looking error instead of the spinner. Consider gating on the projects loading state.

findings.title: Near-duplicate test bodies
findings.body: `test_get_with_error` and `test_get_with_error_context_disabled` repeat about 60 lines of setup: store_event, store_replays, and the recording segment. Move the setup into a helper, or parametrize on the query param, so the two tests differ only in the request and the assertions.

contracts.before_after: The endpoint queries the replay's error_ids, then skips fetch_error_details when enable_error_context is 'false'. The test passes 'false' and asserts the error text is absent from the Seer payload.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** Two probable bugs in the replay summarize endpoint's new error merging: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can pair an ID with the wrong event, and error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay timestamps (probably milliseconds). Smaller issues: the browser-report serializer does not enforce `age`/`timestamp` exclusivity, the dashboard table widget renders empty under its feature flag, and the PR-comment environment lookup costs a query per issue. The no-op'd migrations point to an existing 0921 migration. The other changes looked fine.

**Batch 1 of 4, retry.** I found two issues, both at "consider". The first is that `chart.tsx` renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with empty columns and data when `use-table-widget-visualization` is on. The second is that `commit_context.py` calls `get_recommended_event` once per issue when building the PR comment. I did not run any code, and my reading was limited. I checked the flagged hunk, the `groupingVariant.tsx` imports, the `delayed_workflow.py` accessors, and searched `src` for the flag. I skimmed the other files from the diff. I did not fill in `contracts`, so the contract and bounded-wait questions are unanswered.

**Batch 2 of 4.** I found one bug in this part. In `attributes.tsx`, the new hidden-attribute filter only runs when the user has typed a search query, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still show in the default view. I only read `attributes.tsx` and the `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` call sites. I did not read the other files in this part in full. I found nothing else wrong in the `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` refactor. Its one consumer, `traceItemAttributeContext.tsx`, only spreads the returned attributes, so an `undefined` value is safe there.

**Batch 2 of 4, retry.** I found nothing to flag in this part. The Explore `Visualize` change from `yAxes` to a single `yAxis` is consistent across the call sites. `getVisualizesFromLocation` already produced one `Visualize` per y-axis, so the old multi-axis loops were effectively dead. Writable page params still use `BaseVisualize` and `yAxes`, and `isBaseVisualize` matches that shape. The new `TableWidgetVisualization` and its stories are consistent with the fixture. I didn't build or run anything.

**Batch 3 of 4.** This part is mostly Flex refactors and test updates, and I found nothing that blocks the merge. I read the code the specs depend on: `Visualize` and `BaseVisualize`, `useGetTraceItemAttributeValues`, the editor modal's `handleApply`, `MatchedRow` in the replay delete usecase, and `useProjectFromId`. The specs match the current code. The one finding is a low-confidence "consider" on `static/app/views/replays/detail/ai/index.tsx`: it may flash a "Project not found" alert while projects are still loading.

**Batch 4 of 4.** The test changes in this part look correct against the code they exercise, with one cleanup suggestion. Two replay tests duplicate about 60 lines of setup.
